Title: Benjamin Cooper Memorial Lecture
Description: Join us for the 29th annual Benjamin Cooper Memorial Lecture. The Benjamin Cooper Memorial Lecture was established in memory of Ben Cooper by his close friends David Goldberg '98, Jennifer Miller '98, Megan Palmer '97, Jacob Remes '98, Dan Sharfman '97, & Jessica Wolland '97. Ben, a rising senior at Georgetown Day School, was killed in a tragic accident on August 12, 1997. The Lecture Fund, endowed by the Cooper-Areen family, enables GDS to bring a renowned guest lecturer to the school each year

The session will start together, followed by breakouts based on the assessments given at various grade levels.

Title: A Celebration of the 1945 Society at Georgetown Day School

Named for the year in which GDS was founded, the 1945 Society was established to provide our School’s philanthropic leaders the opportunity to express their dedication & commitment to the founding families’ vision, ideals, & principles. Members of the 1945 Society, & those who volunteered last year to secure foundational philanthropic support for the School, will be celebrated at a reception hosted by the HoS & BoT.

All new-to-GDS 10th, 11th and 12th graders will gather for a chance to meet each other, learn about the culture of the high school, connect with some current students, meet with staff (teachers, deans, administrators), and get familiar with the building before the first day of school.
 
 Questions? Please email dpardner@gds.org.

Title: Orientation Family Cook-out
Description: 9th Grade families are invited to the High School for a family cook-out.

Title: Opening Days and New Faculty & Staff Orientation
9th Grade Picture Day
Description: All 9th graders will have their pictures taken during Orientation for student IDs, MyGDS, the yearbook, and for school portraits, which families can later purchase. A make-up day will follow for those who miss picture day or families who are not pleased with their portraits.

Title: Opening Days and New Faculty & Staff Orientation
Hop-Into-GDS Bridge Program
Description:
Hop-Into-GDS Bridge Program. We invite new-to-GDS 9th graders to join us for our Hop-Into-GDS Program, intended to give students new to GDS a preview of life within the High School community. The goals of this program are to expose and introduce students to the GDS High School experience and to develop a cohort of students who are able to grow together as a community before 9th grade orientation begins.
 
Email scordo@gds.org with questions.

Title: General Information Session about Transportation Options Session #2
Description:
Do you have questions about our commute to GDS for Fall, 2026? Join one of our upcoming info sessions. During these sessions, we will talk through the various options and restrictions related to commuting to GDS and answer questions that you might have. We will also be able to help you determine what commuting method is best for your family. If you have any questions, please contact: ImproveMyCommute@gds.org.
Meeting Link: https://gds-org.zoom.us/j/2679759863?pwd=awpLpm9zYEETjxXLU3ogZRrDcVyDqE.1

Title: GDS 360 Season 1 Registration Opens
Description:
Don't forget to enroll in the exciting enrichment class offerings from the GDS 360 Extended Day Program! Classes fill quickly, so register early. Families receiving financial aid should check their emails for a financial aid code from the GDS 360 team. Register at gds360.campbrainregistration.com.
 
 Questions? Please email auxiliaryprograms@gds.org

Title: Dinner and Conversations with Antonio "Tony" Harris
Description: The Office of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion invites you to a Dinner & Conversation featuring our beloved member of the GDS community and security team, Antonio “Tony” Harris, who will share his "Voice of a Survivor of a School Shooting" presentation to the community.
LocationDisplay: LMS > B201 LMS Flexible Performance Center

Title: Parent Showcase for Upper Level Historic Research Seminar: Race, Place, and Real Estate
CMD Kick Off Meeting
Description:
Join us for our final PSA meeting of the year and kick off plans for CMD 2026! 

Next year’s Country Market Day will take place on Saturday, September 26, 2026, in conjunction with Sports Saturday.

Whether you’re a returning volunteer or new to CMD/PSA, we would love your ideas, energy, and support as we kick off planning for next school year. So that we have a headcount for breakfast, please RSVP before May 10. We look forward to seeing you there!

Title: Black Alumni Brunch
Description:
Join us at Ben’s Next Door from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. as we close out reunion weekend with the annual Black Alumni Brunch. Due to venue capacity, space is limited. Must be 21 or older.
https://www.gds.org/alumni/reunion-2026/rsvp

Title: Navigating College Admissions: First Generation Parents and Guardians
Description:
Join us for an informative presentation and open Q&A session about the U.S. college admissions process. This program is designed especially for parents and guardians who did not attend college themselves or who completed their education outside of the United States.

If you are supporting a child through the U.S. college application process for the first time, this session will provide clear guidance, practical information, and the opportunity to ask questions of the GDS College Counseling team

Title: Ninth and Tenth Grade College Counseling Meet and Greet
Description: The College Counseling Office will introduce ninth and tenth parents and guardians to the college counseling program at GDS. We will provide information about the arc of the college counseling process at GDS, standardized testing, and college admissions.

Title: Former Faculty and Current Parent Alumni Luncheon
Description: Current parent Alumni (CPALs) and former faculty and staff are invited to this luncheon to reconnect and hear updates about the school. Current faculty and staff are encouraged to stop by as their schedules allow. Did receive an invite? Email alumni@gds.org

Title: State of the School & Parent Corporation Meeting
Description: Parents are invited to join us for this evening session, in which Head of School Russell Shaw will give an overview of where the school stands for the 2025-26 school year. The State of the School presentation will be followed by our annual Parent Corporation Meeting held by the Board of Trustees.

Title: 3rd & 4th Grade Parent Coffee
Description: As we begin the third trimester. Join us to learn about the exciting learning your child will embark on for the remainder of the year. We will begin each session by sharing how Lower School is incorporating "The Writing Revolution" into its writing instruction. Following, we will break out into grade levels where you will hear from the Grade Level Leads, a member of the VPA team, and more!

Title: Parent Connect: for Adoptive Parents
Description:
Join the counselors and Debbie Riley, LCMFT, and CEO at the Center for Adoption Support and Education during National Adoption Awareness Month. Debbie and a panel of adult adoptees will share experiences and offer support for adoptive parents. Families and student support team members from other nearby independent schools are also invited.

Please contact Meryl Heyliger with questions: mheyliger@gds.org

Title: Fancy Sparkly Day
Description: Fancy Sparkly Day is a GDS event where all community members are invited to arrive at school in attire that makes them feel beautiful, but especially things they consider extra fancy or sparkly. Students are invited to participate in a fun, music-filled parade celebrating their individuality.

Title: Stephanie Burt '89: Taylor Swift at Harvard, the Future of Poetry, and Other Mild Surprises
Description: Harvard Professor Stephanie Burt '89, who drew national attention for her course on Taylor Swift, will be speaking on campus about her new book, Taylor's Version, and her journey from GDS student to renowned poet and literary critic.

Title: [PSA] Coffee for Families Effected by Government Shutdown
Description: Please join us for coffee and discussion for parents and guardians  impacted by federal layoffs, funding cuts, and the government shutdown (even if your impact is psychological or emotional). This Thursday morning 10/9 at 8:30am in the cafe.

Title: High School History Speaker Series
Description: Marcia Chatelain is a scholar, speaker, and strategist based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania and Washington, D.C. When she's not in the classroom, she's on the road, talking to audiences about our nation’s pressing and pervasive social issues, including racism, universities and the history of slavery, as well as activist movements.
